title: RAW UNREVIEWED: fixed covering-layer semantics restricts a later direct-contact patient
summary: An already-priced nonpenetrating covering operation predicts that later direct physical contact reaches the exposed outer layer rather than a buried earlier deposit. This concerns contact accessibility, not previous-layer visibility or owner capacity.

design.mechanism: On the same already-bound substrate, deposit A then B. Only if fixed paid semantics explicitly make B a complete nonpenetrating cover does direct contact select B or its exposed surface. Contact with buried A requires a written already-priced removal or exposure action.
design.contrast: Ordered covering-layer account versus a fixed mixture account without separate exposed and buried interfaces.
design.prediction: Apply unchanged meanings, interface assumptions and grammar to both complete contexts; a later direct-contact consumer cannot silently reach the buried deposit. Transparent, porous, incomplete or diffused layers are retained counterexamples and outside eligibility unless their consequences are already priced.
design.scope: No additional glosses, local material properties or motion repair.

required_falsifier: Reject the covering branch if its whole graph directs physical contact to a buried layer without a written exposure operation, or needs changed interface assumptions between contexts. If covering/contact semantics were not already paid, leave proposal unselected.
exact_changed_research_decision: A fully priced layer hypothesis must predict accessibility of the later contact patient before any lexical extension; visibility alone cannot justify accessibility.
